name: Proxmox_VE_Node_Network
description: State of this Proxmox VE node's bridges, the virtual switches its guests attach to, and of the VLANs its guests use on them, asked of the node itself.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript: one /nodes/{node}/network call to this node per interval. Discovery, hourly, also reads this node's guest lists and each guest's config, which needs VM.Audit (PVEAuditor holds it); a config it cannot read costs that guest's VLANs only, and the next hourly run tries again.

Instances: one per bridge, Linux or Open vSwitch (types bridge and OVSBridge), its wildvalue the bridge name; and one per VLAN a guest NIC on this node uses (a NIC with tag=N), its wildvalue <bridge>-vlan<N>, in the instance group vlan. A bridge name that is an SDN VNet is left to Proxmox_VE_Cluster_SDN. trunks= is not a VLAN of its own. Physical ports, bonds and host VLAN interfaces are not discovered: the node's own SNMP interface monitoring covers its ports with link state, speed, traffic and errors.

Active is Proxmox's own flag. Healthy is 0 only for a bridge set to start at boot (autostart) that is not active -- the guests on it have lost their network -- so a bridge left down on purpose is not an alert. Ports counts the bridge's ports. A VLAN reports its bridge's Active, and neither Healthy nor Ports: Proxmox gives a VLAN no state of its own, so only the bridge alerts -- one alert for a bridge that goes down, not one more per VLAN on it. On a VLAN instance the Bridge Ports graph and the Bridge State graph's Healthy line stay empty, and Raw Data shows those two datapoints as not found: by design, not a collection fault. LogicMonitor's Dependent Alert Mapping works on resources, not instances, so it would not have folded those copies together. Collection learns which VLANs exist from the instances LogicMonitor passes a BatchScript (datasourceinstanceProps), so a poll stays one call.

Each instance carries a topology vertex for Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Topology (predef.externalResourceID and predef.externalResourceType), type VirtualSwitch: node to bridge to guest, or node to bridge to VLAN to guest for a tagged NIC. A VLAN is this node's alone, since Proxmox cannot say that VLAN 30 on two nodes is one segment. Where topo.namespace or topo.blacklist is set, which rewrites the TopologySource's keys, discovery stamps none. The map's Connections filter hides every Network edge at once.

A VLAN no guest uses any more keeps its instance, as everything this suite discovers does: it drops off the map, still reports its bridge's Active, and is deleted by hand.

Applies on ProxmoxVE_Node resources the NetScan has not marked unreachable (pve.netscan.reachable). The node is asked directly, at this resource's own hostname, and never through another node: another node would answer for itself. The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

datapoints.name: Active
datapoints.description: 1 when Proxmox reports the bridge active. A VLAN reports its bridge's value.

datapoints.name: Healthy
datapoints.description: 0 when the bridge is set to start at boot but is not active; 1 otherwise. Bridges only: a VLAN reports its bridge's Active instead, so a bridge outage alerts once.
datapoints.alertBody:
Bridge ##INSTANCE## on ##HOST## is set to start at boot but is not active: the guests on it, on every VLAN of it, have no network.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: Ports
datapoints.description: The number of ports configured on the bridge. Not reported for a VLAN.
